## Architecture thesis

DeadReckon is an outer supervisory harness around inner coding harnesses. The inner harness supplies intelligence and mutation; DeadReckon owns the operational boundary: workspace isolation, provider routing, budgets, cancellation, durable evidence, independent acceptance, promotion, and later lifecycle actions. That product boundary is explicit in the purpose statement ([PRODUCT.md:14](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/PRODUCT.md:14)) and in the two provider execution modes below.

## Component map

| Layer | Responsibility | Key evidence |
|---|---|---|
| `deadreckon` binary | Clap surface, guided `start`, direct `run`, orchestration, campaigns, chains, attach/TUI, lifecycle, inspection, import/learning | The dispatcher maps the large command tree into private command families ([main.rs:596](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon/src/main.rs:596), [commands/mod.rs:1](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon/src/commands/mod.rs:1)). |
| `deadreckon-runtime` | The bounded turn loop, provider flight recorder, compaction, docs polish, composable seams | Public surface is intentionally small ([runtime/lib.rs:4](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon-runtime/src/lib.rs:4)); the loop composes core, providers, and sandbox ([turn_loop.rs:14](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon-runtime/src/turn_loop.rs:14)). |
| `deadreckon-core` | Durable domain model and mechanics: state, locks, runs, plans, chains, campaigns, artifacts, docs, gate/tamper, promotion, learning, shared `RunView` | Module/re-export map ([core/lib.rs:4](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon-core/src/lib.rs:4)). This is the real domain kernel, though it now owns many distinct subsystems. |
| `deadreckon-providers` | Common `Provider` trait, fallback router, HTTP adapters, native Codex/Claude adapters, descriptor-driven generic CLIs, Codex app-server steering | Request/response/trait contract ([types.rs:89](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon-providers/src/types.rs:89), [types.rs:141](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon-providers/src/types.rs:141), [types.rs:174](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon-providers/src/types.rs:174)). |
| `deadreckon-sandbox` | Backend resolution, profiles/argv, tool policy, process execution and cancellation | Facade ([sandbox/lib.rs:4](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon-sandbox/src/lib.rs:4)); backends are Seatbelt, Bubblewrap, Docker, or none ([backend.rs:44](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon-sandbox/src/backend.rs:44)). |
| `deadreckon-protocol` | Pure persisted-wire vocabulary for run ledgers; no I/O or internal dependency | Dependency law is stated in code ([protocol/lib.rs:4](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon-protocol/src/lib.rs:4)) and guarded by test ([dependency_law.rs:5](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon-protocol/tests/dependency_law.rs:5)). This is an active migration, not yet the fully landed architecture. |
| Markdown skills | Agent-facing judgment/prompt behavior, kept outside the binary invariant layer | A run records and resolves a selected skill path; user skills override repository skills ([state.rs:180](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon-core/src/state.rs:180), [state.rs:211](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon-core/src/state.rs:211)). |

Dependency direction is effectively:

`deadreckon CLI → runtime → providers + sandbox + core → protocol`

There are small architectural leaks: providers depends on core for capability/steering types, and sandbox depends on core for I/O retry classification ([providers/types.rs:6](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon-providers/src/types.rs:6), [sandbox/backend.rs:4](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon-sandbox/src/backend.rs:4)).

## The harness-of-harness abstraction

There are two materially different engines behind the same `Provider::complete` interface:

- Direct API routes return one JSON action (`bash`, `write_file`, inert `reshape`, or `done`) per outer turn. DeadReckon parses and executes those actions itself ([turn_loop.rs:123](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon-runtime/src/turn_loop.rs:123), [turn_loop.rs:671](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon-runtime/src/turn_loop.rs:671)).
- CLI routes receive a complete sub-agent prompt and mutate the working directory directly. DeadReckon then detects changed files, snapshots, commits, records provenance, runs docs/gate, and promotes ([turn_loop.rs:259](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon-runtime/src/turn_loop.rs:259), [turn_loop.rs:549](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon-runtime/src/turn_loop.rs:549), [turn_loop.rs:1162](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon-runtime/src/turn_loop.rs:1162)).

The provider registry is the extensibility mechanism: built-in TOML descriptors plus `~/.deadreckon/providers.d/*.toml` overrides ([registry/mod.rs:441](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon-providers/src/registry/mod.rs:441)). Generic CLI descriptors can declare argv, sandbox access, model catalog, auth probes, ingest, and structured wire contracts; the generic driver has both contract-aware and compatible raw-output paths ([cli_generic.rs:20](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon-providers/src/cli_generic.rs:20), [cli_generic.rs:70](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon-providers/src/cli_generic.rs:70)).

This is the essential abstraction to preserve: new intelligence sources fit behind `Provider`; DeadReckon’s trust boundary does not move.

## Single-run end-to-end path

1. `run` resolves config/provider/model/docs, done criteria, sandbox, and source mode; it refuses hollow detected contracts unless explicitly overridden ([commands/run.rs:72](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon/src/commands/run.rs:72), [commands/run.rs:179](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon/src/commands/run.rs:179), [commands/run.rs:268](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon/src/commands/run.rs:268)).
2. Default source mode is an isolated Git worktree when possible; the command creates the worktree, durable run, acceptance copy, and scoped lock ([commands/run.rs:321](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon/src/commands/run.rs:321), [commands/run.rs:324](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon/src/commands/run.rs:324), [commands/run.rs:357](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon/src/commands/run.rs:357)).
3. `create_run` creates working/snapshot/gate directories, a run-local nonce, initial docs, codebase record, atomic state, and current pointer ([state.rs:195](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon-core/src/state.rs:195)).
4. The loop loads history, writes the resolved seam audit, arms cancellation, sets execution phase, snapshots before every turn, builds the prompt, and calls the router ([turn_loop.rs:171](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon-runtime/src/turn_loop.rs:171), [turn_loop.rs:222](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon-runtime/src/turn_loop.rs:222)).
5. Provider calls are bounded by remaining wall time and get one fixed two-second retry on transient failure ([turn_loop.rs:301](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon-runtime/src/turn_loop.rs:301), [turn_loop.rs:311](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon-runtime/src/turn_loop.rs:311)).
6. Every successful turn appends trace, spend, token/spend events, snapshots, provenance, docs checkpoints, and per-turn Git commits for worktree mode ([turn_loop.rs:459](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon-runtime/src/turn_loop.rs:459), [turn_loop.rs:477](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon-runtime/src/turn_loop.rs:477), [turn_loop.rs:792](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon-runtime/src/turn_loop.rs:792)).
7. A model’s `done` is only a proposal: implementation notes must be current, docs are completed, `dr-gate` is launched as a sibling binary, and a failed check feeds corrective history back into the loop ([turn_loop.rs:986](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon-runtime/src/turn_loop.rs:986), [turn_loop.rs:1978](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon-runtime/src/turn_loop.rs:1978), [turn_loop.rs:2087](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon-runtime/src/turn_loop.rs:2087), [turn_loop.rs:2111](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon-runtime/src/turn_loop.rs:2111)).
8. `dr-gate` evaluates all checks, evaluates tampering, refuses failed required checks, then writes the marker ([dr-gate.rs:28](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon/src/bin/dr-gate.rs:28)). Validation binds marker to run, pass status, producer, nonce-derived signature, checks, and tamper record ([gate.rs:125](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon-core/src/gate.rs:125), [gate.rs:751](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon-core/src/gate.rs:751)).
9. Promotion re-validates the marker, stages/copies or renames the result, writes a provenance-bound manifest, atomically renames into the library, and records the library path ([promotion.rs:27](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon-core/src/promotion.rs:27)).

One notable policy detail: `run` currently supplies `max_turns: 12` as a code constant, not config ([commands/run.rs:482](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon/src/commands/run.rs:482)).

## Persistence and observability

Runtime home defaults to `~/.deadreckon`; it contains config, scoped runstate/current pointers, locks, plans, chains, library, and learning data ([paths.rs:6](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon-core/src/paths.rs:6), [paths.rs:51](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon-core/src/paths.rs:51), [paths.rs:71](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon-core/src/paths.rs:71), [paths.rs:83](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon-core/src/paths.rs:83), [paths.rs:147](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon-core/src/paths.rs:147)).

State writes use temp-file, fsync, then persist; JSONL appends are also fsynced ([state.rs:465](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon-core/src/state.rs:465), [state.rs:487](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon-core/src/state.rs:487)). Locks combine an OS file lock with durable heartbeat/PID metadata and will not usurp a live owner merely because its heartbeat is stale ([lock.rs:91](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon-core/src/lock.rs:91), [lock.rs:128](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon-core/src/lock.rs:128)).

Events are always appended before optional same-process broadcast ([events.rs:37](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon-core/src/events.rs:37)); attach can therefore use broadcast locally or tail/replay JSONL across processes ([tui_events.rs:15](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon/src/tui_events.rs:15), [tui_events.rs:46](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon/src/tui_events.rs:46)). `RunView` is the shared file-backed projection over state, ledgers, proof, sandbox, diffs, docs, and missing artifacts used to keep inspection surfaces coherent ([run_view.rs:22](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon-core/src/run_view.rs:22), [run_view.rs:47](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon-core/src/run_view.rs:47)).

## Multi-run execution paths

- `start` is the guided course selector; it chooses a single run, review plan, full plan, or campaign and records a launch plan.
- `orchestrate review` creates coder then reviewer tasks; `full-plan` asks a planner for a dependency graph. The wrapper is literally create plan → fork → merge ([orchestrate.rs:459](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon/src/commands/orchestrate.rs:459)).
- Plan fork executes dependency-ready tasks in waves and runs ready children concurrently ([plan.rs:235](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon-core/src/plan.rs:235), [commands/plan.rs:1687](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon/src/commands/plan.rs:1687)). Each child is another `deadreckon run`/`extend` subprocess with isolated scope and normal gate semantics ([commands/plan.rs:2645](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon/src/commands/plan.rs:2645), [commands/plan.rs:2728](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon/src/commands/plan.rs:2728)).
- Merge refuses incomplete children, composes DAG-aware results, optionally launches bounded repair for conflicts, then creates a synthetic merged run and consolidated docs ([merge.rs:19](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon/src/commands/merge.rs:19), [merge.rs:67](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon/src/commands/merge.rs:67), [merge.rs:189](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon/src/commands/merge.rs:189)).
- Campaign is a meta-coordinator: one root goal becomes N independent full-plan sub-orchestrators, capped at depth two, with lineage/cycle controls and leaf-verdict roll-up ([campaign.rs:1](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon-core/src/campaign.rs:1), [campaign.rs:21](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon-core/src/campaign.rs:21), [campaign.rs:140](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon-core/src/campaign.rs:140)).
- Chain is serial composition: a conductor runs normal gated runs one at a time, accumulates budget/wall totals, invokes hooks, and applies or pauses according to policy ([chain/mod.rs:753](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon/src/commands/chain/mod.rs:753), [chain/mod.rs:839](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon/src/commands/chain/mod.rs:839), [chain/mod.rs:927](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon/src/commands/chain/mod.rs:927)).

## Maturity assessment

### Stable/load-bearing

- Single-run supervision, durable state, worktree/copy modes, provider routing, sandbox execution, cancellation, gate/tamper, promotion, lifecycle, and `RunView` are deeply integrated and should be treated as the essential spine.
- The repo declares version `0.6.0` ([Cargo.toml:12](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/Cargo.toml:12)); `make verify` runs formatting, clippy, public-surface checks, the workspace test suite, and release build ([Makefile:66](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/Makefile:66)).
- Rudder and Pennant are labeled stable: app-server steering/approvals/degradation ([CHANGELOG.md:3](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/CHANGELOG.md:3)) and descriptor-declared CLI contracts ([CHANGELOG.md:34](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/CHANGELOG.md:34)).
- Composable seams are real and bounded: policy, catalog, hooks, and event sink are sandboxed JSON-over-stdio workers; the gate is explicitly non-swappable ([seam.rs:18](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon-runtime/src/seam.rs:18), [seam.rs:167](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon-runtime/src/seam.rs:167), [seam.rs:226](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon-runtime/src/seam.rs:226)).

### Half-built / currently in decision

- Keel is mid-flight. HEAD contains phases P1–P6; the working tree has P7 schema work. The goal requires eleven phases, with reader rewire at P8, writer/re-export cleanup at P9, user surface at P10, and architecture/changelog closure at P11 ([keel-rider.md:135](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/docs/goals/2026-07-11-1121-deadreckon-keel-rider.md:135), [keel-rider.md:147](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/docs/goals/2026-07-11-1121-deadreckon-keel-rider.md:147)). Consequently protocol and core currently coexist as a migration architecture.
- Provider parity remains deliberately uneven. Pi and Copilot have descriptor contracts; Gemini and OpenCode are documented evidence-backed gaps ([AS-BUILT-ARCHITECTURE.md:3734](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/docs/AS-BUILT-ARCHITECTURE.md:3734)). Claude structured output still explicitly proceeds unconstrained ([cli_claude_code.rs:188](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon-providers/src/cli_claude_code.rs:188)).
- Process supervision is not yet process-group safe and capture is whole-buffer. The planned Capstan slice exists specifically because spawned child trees can orphan and large outputs flow unbounded into memory/ledgers ([capstan-goal.md:1](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/docs/goals/2026-07-11-1122-deadreckon-capstan-goal.md:1), [sandbox/process.rs:22](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon-sandbox/src/process.rs:22)).
- Retry/testing determinism is only baseline: one fixed retry exists, while richer Retry-After/backoff and scripted full-loop model tests are still the Drydock goal ([drydock-goal.md:1](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/docs/goals/2026-07-11-1123-deadreckon-drydock-goal.md:1)).
- `auto` sandbox falls back to `none` with a warning if the platform backend is absent ([backend.rs:82](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon-sandbox/src/backend.rs:82)). This is functional but weakens the “sandboxed by default” promise and deserves an explicit product decision.

### Plausible cruft or consolidation candidates

- `acceptance` is explicitly an advanced compatibility surface superseded by `def-done` ([cli.rs:244](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon/src/cli.rs:244)).
- `Materialize` is a hidden compatibility command whose visible names are `export`/`copy-out` ([cli.rs:1387](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon/src/cli.rs:1387)).
- Docs polish retains a legacy single-skill path only for older custom installs ([polish.rs:134](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon-runtime/src/polish.rs:134)).
- The early “as-built” overview is stale: it says version `0.1.0` and five members ([AS-BUILT-ARCHITECTURE.md:3](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/docs/AS-BUILT-ARCHITECTURE.md:3), [AS-BUILT-ARCHITECTURE.md:113](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/docs/AS-BUILT-ARCHITECTURE.md:113)), while the current workspace is `0.6.0` with six members including protocol ([Cargo.toml:1](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/Cargo.toml:1)). Later sections are current, so this is documentation accretion rather than one trustworthy reconstruction.
- The private-module decomposition has not produced a thin CLI layer in practice: core owns many unrelated domains and the binary still centralizes configuration/default extraction and considerable shared behavior ([main.rs:3735](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon/src/main.rs:3735)). This is architectural debt, though not proof that the underlying capabilities are unnecessary.
